summary: Can you reach the last index when nums[i] is the maximum jump length from i?
mainInsight: Track the farthest index reachable so far. Scan left to right: if the current index exceeds the farthest reach, you are stuck (return False); otherwise update reach = max(reach, i + nums[i]). If the reach covers the last index, return True.

approaches.name: DP / recursion with memo
approaches.summary: canReach(i) = any(canReach(j)) for j in i+1..i+nums[i].

commonMistakes: Not stopping when i exceeds the reach
edgeCases: Zero at the first index with n > 1
Zero in the middle that can be jumped over

promptVariants: What single value summarises everything you need while scanning Jump Game?
options: The farthest index reachable so far; if i exceeds it you are stuck
The number of jumps made so far; stop at the last index
The largest value in the array; jump greedily by it
The sum of nums so far; stop when it exceeds n
cards.answer: The farthest index reachable so far; if i exceeds it you are stuck
cards.explanation: If every earlier index reaches less than i, index i is unreachable.

incorrectOptionExplanations.The sum of nums so far; stop when it exc: The sum has no meaning for reachability.

promptVariants: Why is tracking only the farthest reach sufficient?
Why can any index below the reach be used?
cards.answer: From any reachable index you can jump to any smaller distance (nums[i] is a maximum), so all indices up to the farthest reach are reachable. Therefore the set of reachable indices is a prefix [0, reach], and a single number represents it.
keyPoints: Jumps can be shorter than the maximum
cards.explanation: That contiguity is the key insight.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (excluding the input): ___

options: False: nothing can get past index 3, whose jump length is 0
True: index 1 can jump 2 steps to index 3 and then to 4
True: the array has enough total jump length
False: index 0 cannot jump at all
cards.answer: False: nothing can get past index 3, whose jump length is 0
cards.explanation: The farthest reachable index is 3 (from index 1), and index 3 has jump length 0, so index 4 is out of reach.

incorrectOptionExplanations.True: index 1 can jump 2 steps to index: Index 3 has jump length 0, so it cannot continue to index 4.
incorrectOptionExplanations.True: the array has enough total jump le: Total jump length is irrelevant; reachability index by index is what matters.
incorrectOptionExplanations.False: index 0 cannot jump at all: Index 0 can jump one step to index 1.
